subject: english
question:
Choose the correct meaning of idiom:

Not worth his salt

options.text: Undeserving of the pay/respect he gets

solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 4** i.e. "Undeserving of the pay/respect he gets".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"Not worth his salt"** means that someone is not deserving of the pay or respect they receive due to underperformance or lack of contribution. (वह अपने वेतन या सम्मान के योग्य नहीं है)
 
 
• **Example:** If a teacher cannot inspire their students, they are not worth their salt.
 

 
• **Explanation:** In ancient times, salt was a valuable commodity, and Roman soldiers were sometimes paid in salt. The phrase signifies that someone is not earning their pay or respect. (प्राचीन समय में, नमक मूल्यवान था और यह कहावत प्रदर्शन की कमी को दर्शाती है।)

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 1: Lacking in courage** (साहस की कमी) - Refers to someone who is timid or afraid to take risks.
 
 
• **Example:** He was lacking in courage and avoided confronting his boss about the unfair treatment.
 
 

 
• **Option 2: Unable to learn** (सीखने में असमर्थ) - Refers to someone who is slow or unwilling to grasp new concepts.
 
 
• **Example:** No one is completely unable to learn if they put in effort and practice.
 
 

 
• **Option 3: Too proud to work** (काम करने में बहुत गर्व महसूस करना) - Refers to someone who considers working beneath their status.
 
 
• **Example:** Despite losing his wealth, he was too proud to work and ended up in debt.
